title: A Wobbly Space Peanut with a Watery Secret!
summary: Have you ever spun a top and watched it wobble? Now picture a giant space rock doing the same thing — but it's shaped like a peanut! NASA's Lucy spacecraft just visited an asteroid named Donaldjohanson, and what it found is way weirder than anyone expected. First, the shape: it's not a round ball. It's made of two big lumps stuck together by a skinny neck, like a peanut. Scientists call this a bilobate asteroid. It probably formed about 155 million years ago when two chunks from a big crash slowly drifted together. But here's the really cool part: it doesn't just spin like a planet. It tumbles end-over-end once every 10.5 days, and it also rocks back and forth every 26.5 days. Imagine doing a cartwheel while wiggling at the same time! Why does it move so strangely? Sunlight! Over millions of years, tiny pushes from sunlight — called the YORP effect — have slowed its spin and made it wobble. Lucy also spotted signs of ancient water. Its instruments found clay minerals that only form when rock meets liquid water. That means this little asteroid might have been wet long ago. Lucy zipped past at 30,000 miles per hour, snapping pictures and taking measurements. This was a practice run for its bigger mission: visiting Jupiter's Trojan asteroids in 2027. But even a practice run can uncover amazing secrets. Who knew a space peanut could be so exciting?
why_it_matters: Studying wobbling space rocks helps scientists understand how our solar system formed—and one day might even help protect Earth from dangerous asteroids.

Two groups of space rocks that share Jupiter’s path around the Sun.

background_read: NASA’s Lucy space mission launched in 2021 to study ancient asteroids near Jupiter. It is named after the famous fossil skeleton ‘Lucy,’ which taught us a lot about early humans.
The asteroid Donaldjohanson is named after the scientist who discovered that fossil. Jupiter’s Trojan asteroids are two huge swarms of rocks that share the giant planet’s orbit around the Sun.

WHAT: Discovered that asteroid Donaldjohanson is a peanut-shaped, tumbling rock with signs of ancient water

WHY: As a practice run before visiting Jupiter’s Trojan asteroids in 2027

perspectives.description: Every odd movement or water clue teaches us something new about the history of our solar system. This little peanut-shaped asteroid is a time capsule!
It’s just a dusty rock far away. Some people might say spending money on space rocks takes away from problems on Earth, like poverty or disease.
Imagining a giant rock doing cartwheels and wiggles in space makes the universe feel wild and alive. I want to see what Lucy finds next!
